questions.q: With the example of the Indira Gandhi Canal, explain why development must be sustainable.

answer.text: Sustainable development means meeting the needs of the present without harming the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. It requires that economic growth should not damage the environment or exhaust natural resources.

The Indira Gandhi Canal in Rajasthan is a striking example. It brought water for irrigation into the dry desert, allowing farming to spread and transforming the lives of the people. Crops that could never grow before began to flourish, and the region prospered.
However, the excessive and careless use of canal water, without proper drainage, led to serious problems of waterlogging and the spread of salinity, which damaged the very land it had made fertile.
This shows that development must be planned with care for the environment, using proper drainage, suitable crops and eco-development measures.

answer: Thus true development must be ecologically sustainable, balancing growth with the health of the land.
